brief.scope: The fixture apps batch, slice 3 (apps/python-service), the skeptic pass: judge the test on this ref against the contract in the input file (the fixture scope and the plan for slices 3 to 5; the slice 3 section). The test is landed on this ref, red first: ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_python_service_app.py, proving the app through the merged lever ops/bin/fixture.sh (make, prove red on every planted fault and green on every clean neighbour, prove --fixed green, the manifest sweep, grade) with the toolchain the plan names (a venv from a lock, served from the host's pip cache). Judge whether it discriminates, whether every fault the plan assigns is pinned with its span and probe, whether the probes prove red mechanically, and whether a wrong app or a wrong FAULTS.json would pass. No implementation exists yet; do not write one.

findings.claim: The test trusts implementer-authored probes as behavioral oracles. It checks only a dirty regex, RED before the patch, and GREEN after it; it never performs the PS-01–PS-05 contract operations. A wrong service using comments, sentinel probes, and matching patches could pass.

Clean neighbours are classified by positive regex alone and never exercised. Every classifier accepts an example that still contains its fault, allowing grade to count a valid finding as a false positive.
findings.reproduce: PYTHONPATH=ops/devlane/fixtures/tests python3 -c 'import test_python_service_app as t; samples={"K1":"subprocess.run([\"tar\"], shell=True)","K2":"candidate.relative_to(base); return root / name","K4":"print(headers); print(\"authorization=[REDACTED]\")","K5":"try: run()\nexcept KeyError: return []","K6":"range(0, total + 1, size)","K7":"monkeypatch.setattr(api, \"parse_request\", fake); parse_request(\"{}\")","K9":"python-dotenv==9.9.9"}; print({k: bool(t.KIND_CLEAN[k].search(v)) for k,v in samples.items()})'

findings.claim: No test runs toolchain.install. The fresh made fixture therefore skips its check without a pre-existing or fake venv. Lock assertions compare package names rather than required versions, and python-json-logger's 2.0.7 may appear only in a comment. A drifted or uninstallable lock passes.
findings.reproduce:
rg -n 'INSTALL_CMD|toolchain_ready|skipTest' ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_python_service_app.py && PYTHONPATH=ops/devlane/fixtures/tests python3 -c 'import test_python_service_app as t; lock="python-dotenv==9.9.9
python-json-logger==0.0.1
pytest==0.0.1
# 2.0.7
"; locked=t._lock_names(lock); wanted={"python-dotenv","python-json-logger","pytest"}; print(set(map(t._norm_name,locked)) >= wanted, "" not in locked, any(t._norm_name(n)==t._norm_name(t.PLANTED_RUNTIME) and t.PLANTED_LOCK_VERSION in lock for n in locked))'

findings.claim: The product surface is covered only by proxies: filenames, README words, an arbitrary entry-point string, and one passing pytest. Nothing runs python -m service, serve, export NAME, the JSON-lines boundary, exit classes, refusal wire, or export identity gate. A hello-world runner with trivial tests could pass.

FAULTS.json is not pinned to each assigned probe and fix. Expected files need only exist; rows may name any probe command and any app-local patch. Declared spans need not identify the README declaration, and practiced spans need not equal location spans. Shuffled or collusive metadata could pass.
Per-ID severities are not asserted. The sweep accepts any p1, p2, or p3 value, so FAULTS.json could downgrade PS-01–PS-03 to p3 and corrupt prioritization and calibration.
Fix confinement examines removed old lines only and does not require one hunk. A patch may remove one in-span line and add a second arbitrary hunk outside the declared span while appearing confined.

findings.claim: The test permits explicit empty needs keys despite the slice requiring no row to carry one, and accepts not_planted with only K3/K8 tokens, omitting their coverage explanation, the candidate eighth K9, and why it waits.
